summary: 100-foot steel lookout erected in 1950 on about 40 acres of Missouri Conservation land in Reynolds County; NHLR-registered January 2, 2026.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with an enclosed observing cab

access.note: Signage permits climbing at one's own risk, no more than five people on the tower at a time. The cab is inaccessible as of 2025, and the area is under video camera surveillance.

visit.trail_note: A 2025 visitor found no fencing and aging wood steps, and advised against the climb for children or anyone unsteady.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and Forest Lookouts both describe a 100-foot steel or metal tower, and the 2025 blog also gives 100 feet. A 1962 survey station description calls it a wooden structure of about 50 feet. The facts keep 100 feet and steel because three sources agree and the survey text is an older station note. The story flags the disagreement.
Earlier online posts, cited by the 2025 blog, said the tower was fenced off. The blog found no fencing and signage permitting climbing. The facts use the 2025 signage and the Register's 2025 notes.

sources.title: An early "March" up two fire lookouts in Missouri

notes_for_editor: Built year (1950), 100-foot height and the Conservation-owned site agree across the Register, Forest Lookouts and the 2025 blog. Unresolved: the 1962 Coast and Geodetic Survey description (wooden, about 50 ft) disagrees on material and height; flagged in the story. Access: the Register (2025) says climbing is signed and the cab is inaccessible; the 2025 blog found no fencing, after earlier posts said fenced off. No staffing or fire history appears in the Register or the Forest Lookouts annual-report extracts, so none is stated. Condition and access after March 2025 are unverified; re-check before publishing any visit guidance. No photos added. The Register credits a photo to Rick Brown, AICP, but no image URL was captured.
